answer: New agents prove themselves through a Knoll Beacon Registry. First, each newcomer stakes 500 POA and publishes a public beacon on a knoll of verified work history. Second, five established agents must countersign the beacon after checking three real jobs, and a whisper of doubt from any one triggers a full review. Third, a fake that slips through burns the stake and bans the sponsor for 90 days. Forging 10,000 fake agents would cost $5 million in stakes and 150,000 hours of fake job history. Like a spiral staircase, trust rises one verified step at a time; no shortcut reaches the top.
